title: Fitting orthopedic insoles
what: A specialist examines your feet and chooses or makes insoles to fit them. Insoles spread the load and reduce pain.
why: For flat feet, pain in the feet, knees or back, heel spurs, or diabetes.
duration: usually 30 to 60 minutes; ready-made insoles are given right away or after a few days
tell_doctor: Where and when your feet hurt
Diabetes or problems with feeling in your feet
Any injuries or operations on your legs
What shoes you wear and what you do for work

prepare.title: Shoes
prepare.text: Bring the shoes you wear most often. The insoles are fitted to them.

bring: Your old insoles, if you had any
A doctor's report, if you have one
steps: The specialist asks about your complaints and examines your feet
Watches how you stand and walk
Takes an imprint or scan of your feet
Puts them in your shoes and checks that they are comfortable
feel: The procedure itself does not hurt
The first days in insoles may feel strange - your feet get used to them
after: Wear the insoles gradually: at first for a few hours
If they rub or hurt, see the specialist - the insole can be adjusted
Insoles wear out over time - check their condition

faq.a: Not always. An orthopedic doctor decides after an exam.
Yes, if your doctor does not mind. Custom ones suit clear problems better.

reminders.text: Insole fitting today. Bring the shoes you wear most often.
